text_solutions.text:
"

Explanation: In Grasshoppers (and some other insects), the mechanism of sex determination follows the XX-XY system where:

  • Females are XX and produce eggs with both X chromosomes.
  • Males are XO (the second sex chromosome is absent in males), and they produce two types of gametes: one with an X chromosome and one without (i.e., an O chromosome).

Now, let's break down the statements:

  • (A) It is an example of female heterogamety.
    • This is incorrect because female heterogamety occurs when females produce two types of gametes (e.g., ZW system in birds, where females are ZW). In Grasshoppers, females are homogametic (XX), meaning they produce one type of gamete, while males are heterogametic (XO), meaning they produce two types of gametes.
  • (B) Females are homogamety (ZZ). 
  • (C) Total number of chromosomes (autosomes and sex chromosomes) is the same in both males and females.
    • This is incorrect. In Grasshoppers, females have XX chromosomes, and males have XO chromosomes, so the total number of chromosomes differs between males and females due to the presence or absence of the second X chromosome in males.
  • (D) All eggs bear an additional X chromosome besides the autosomes.
    • This is correct. Since females are XX, all their eggs will carry one X chromosome.
Final Answer : (1)"

learning_objectives: "<div style=\"text-align:justify\">If DNA is inserted within the coding sequence of enzyme galactosidase
which of the following will occur in case of non-recombinants:-<\/div>\n"

text_solutions.text:
"Explaining : This question is based on the blue-white screening method used in recombinant DNA technology.
Key Concepts: 
  • The lacZ gene encodes β-galactosidase, an enzyme that breaks down lactose and lactose-like analogs.
  • A chromogenic substrate like X-gal (5-bromo-4-chloro-3-indolyl β-D-galactopyranoside) is used.
  • β-galactosidase cleaves X-gal, producing a blue-colored product.
  • Recombinant plasmids have the foreign DNA inserted into the lacZ gene, disrupting it → no functional enzyme → no blue color.
  • Non-recombinant plasmids do not have DNA inserted → intact lacZ gene → active β-galactosidase → cleaves X-gal → blue colonies.

    So, in this question:

  • Non-recombinants = No DNA inserted = lacZ gene is intact
  • Therefore, functional β-galactosidase is produced
  • When grown on a medium with X-gal, colonies appear blue.

  •  Why other options are incorrect:

  • (1) Insertional inactivation → Occurs in recombinants, not non-recombinants.
  • (2) Colonies do not produce any colour → This happens with recombinant colonies (no β-galactosidase).
  • (4) Inactivation of enzyme galactosidase → Again, this is true for recombinants, not non-recombinants. 
Final Answer: (3)"
